title: Associated and weakly associated points at a finitely generated stalk
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let x be a point of X, with local ring O_{X,x} and stalk F_x [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Call x an associated point of F if the maximal ideal m_x of O_{X,x} is an associated prime of the O_{X,x}-module F_x, i.e. m_x = Ann(s) for some s in F_x (Stacks Tag 02OJ), and a weakly associated point of F if m_x is a weakly associated prime of F_x, i.e. m_x is minimal among the prime ideals of O_{X,x} containing Ann(s) for some s in F_x (Stacks Tag 0546). If m_x is finitely generated, then x is an associated point of F if and only if x is a weakly associated point of F.

source.place: Tag 05AR (Lemma 31.5.8, first assertion; proof cites Algebra Lemma 10.66.9)

proof.text: By the definitions of associated and weakly associated point, both predicates at x are exactly the corresponding predicates for the maximal ideal m_x on the local ring O_{X,x} and the module F_x. The stalk and local ring are the objects specified in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

If m_x = Ann(s) for some s in F_x, then m_x is minimal among the prime ideals containing Ann(s), because it is itself that prime ideal. Thus an associated point is weakly associated; this is the easy implication in Tag 05AR.

For the converse, set R = O_{X,x}, M = F_x, and p = m_x. The hypothesis that x is weakly associated says that p is weakly associated to M. Since p is finitely generated, apply [lem-sc-ass-weakass-fg-prime], the ring/module statement of Algebra Lemma 10.66.9 (Tag 058A), to conclude that p is the annihilator of an element of M. By the definition in step 1, x is associated to F. This uses exactly the local ring, stalk module, and finite generation already present in the item; no Noetherian hypothesis is added.
